t: The Signature Session Standard: Named Sessions, Documented Layouts
title: The Signature Session Standard: Named Sessions, Documented Layouts
description: The Signature standard names every tmux session project-purpose (vision-train, llm-serve) and documents the window/pane layout in the project's TERMINAL.md — anyone (or any future you) recreates the control room in minutes. The standard is in the project template. Sessions become team infrastructure, not personal habit.

demo.program:
print("Sessions: project-purpose names (vision-train, llm-serve).")
print("TERMINAL.md per project: window/pane layout documented.")
print("In project template: sessions = team infrastructure, not habit.")

title: Signature Training-Watch Convention
description: The Signature convention for training sessions: window 1 = run + logs, window 2 = monitors, window 3 = scratch, session named for the experiment, and a WATCHME file in the run dir noting what to check. Anyone attaching knows the layout and what matters. The convention turns 'check my training' from a favor into a procedure.

demo.program:
print("Layout: run+logs | monitors | scratch. Session = experiment name.")
print("WATCHME file: what to check. Attaching = knowing layout + priorities.")
print("'Check my training': from favor to procedure.")

title: Signature vs Ad-Hoc Terminal Use
description: Ad-hoc: default configs, unnamed sessions, four overlapping windows, lost scrollback, 'which shell was training in?'. Signature: standard configs, named sessions, documented layouts, searchable history, recreation recipes. Same terminals — the Signature adds the organization that turns typing into control.

demo.program:
print("Ad-hoc: defaults, unnamed, overlapping, lost. 'Which shell was training?'")
print("Signature: standard configs, named, documented, searchable, recipes.")
print("Same terminals. Organization: typing -> control.")

title: Signature Log-Tailing Conventions
description: The Signature convention tails logs with context: 'tail -f' in the log pane, grep patterns for errors in the copy-mode search, and log files named run-YYYY-MM-DD.log per experiment. Finding what happened is a procedure (pane 2, search 'ERROR') not an excavation. Logs are evidence; the convention makes them accessible evidence.

demo.program:
print("Log pane: tail -f. Search: copy-mode /ERROR. Files: run-YYYY-MM-DD.log.")
print("'What happened' = pane 2 + search, not excavation.")
print("Logs are evidence: convention makes them accessible.")

title: Signature Disconnect-Proof Checklist
description: The Signature checklist before any long run: in tmux? (yes), session named? logs to file? (tee), checkpointing on? WATCHME written? notifications set? Five checks, one minute — the difference between 'the training died with my laptop' and 'the training never noticed'. The checklist is taped to the monitor until it's habit.

demo.program:
checks = ["in tmux?", "session named?", "logs to file (tee)?", "checkpointing on?", "WATCHME written?"]
for c in checks:
    print(f"  [ ] {c}")
print("1 minute: 'died with laptop' vs 'never noticed'. Tape to monitor till habit.")

title: Signature Multi-Box Session Map
description: For the desktop + GPU-box duo, the Signature session map shows which sessions live where (edit locally, train on gpu1, serve on gpu2) in the project's TERMINAL.md. The map prevents the 'wait, where is that running' confusion that multi-machine work breeds. Two machines, one map, zero confusion.

demo.program:
print("TERMINAL.md: session map (edit:local, train:gpu1, serve:gpu2).")
print("'Where is that running?' -> check the map.")
print("Multi-machine without multi-confusion.")

print("Pass: <10 min. Standard -> muscle memory, not unread docs.")
